Mazie Hirono was born on November 3, 1947, in [Fukushima Prefecture](/wiki/Fukushima_Prefecture "Fukushima Prefecture"), Japan to Laura Chie Satō, a Japanese American, and Hirono Matabe, a Japanese veteran of World War II. Laura decided to return to Hawaii with Mazie and one of Mazie's brothers in March 1955. Hirono never saw her father again before he died.[[4]](#cite_note-4) Laura became a newspaper proofreader in 1961 and retired from the Hawaii Newspaper Agency in 1986.[[5]](#cite_note-starbulletin1999-5)[[6]](#cite_note-6)

Raised in [Honolulu](/wiki/Honolulu "Honolulu"), Hirono became a [naturalized](/wiki/Naturalization "Naturalization") U.S. citizen in 1959.[[7]](#cite_note-7) She graduated from [Kaimuki High School](/wiki/Kaimuki_High_School "Kaimuki High School"), which had a predominantly Japanese American student body at the time. Hirono then enrolled at the [University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa](/wiki/University_of_Hawai%CA%BBi_at_M%C4%81noa "University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa"), graduating [Phi Beta Kappa](/wiki/Phi_Beta_Kappa "Phi Beta Kappa") with a [Bachelor of Arts](/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts") in [psychology](/wiki/Psychology "Psychology") in 1970.[[8]](#cite_note-8) She later attended [Georgetown University Law Center](/wiki/Georgetown_University_Law_Center "Georgetown University Law Center") in Washington, D.C., where she obtained her [Juris Doctor](/wiki/Juris_Doctor "Juris Doctor") in 1978. Hirono then returned to Honolulu, where she practiced law.[[9]](#cite_note-9)

Five years after Blofeld's imprisonment, Bond is retired and living in Jamaica when Felix Leiter and his colleague Logan Ash enlist his help in searching for the missing MI6 scientist, Valdo Obruchev. Bond eventually accepts Leiter's request and follows his leads about the scientist's whereabouts to Cuba, where he infiltrates a Spectre gathering. Obruchev realises that it is a trap set by Blofeld to kill Bond with a deadly [nanoscale weapon](/wiki/Nanobot "Nanobot"), but he is working for someone else and has re-engineered the weapon to attack only the members of Spectre. When Bond brings Obruchev to Leiter, Ash betrays them and helps Obruchev escape, killing Leiter. Bond returns to MI6 and confronts M regarding the development of the weapon, known as "Heracles", a nanobot that can be programmed to attack specific people based on their genetic markers. He then visits Blofeld in prison and is reacquainted with Madeleine Swann. Swann decides to leave before Blofeld arrives, while Bond has an altercation with Blofeld, who dies soon after. It is revealed that when he touched Swann, Bond was infected with Heracles nanobots that were programmed to kill Blofeld.

Bond traces Swann back to her childhood home where she is living with her five-year-old daughter, Mathilde. She tells Bond about Lyutsifer Safin, the man who controls Heracles. After Bond avenges Leiter's death by killing Ash, Safin captures Swann and Mathilde and brings them to his island, which is the Heracles factory. Bond works with MI6 to rescue Swann and Mathilde and destroy Safin's factory with a missile strike launched from a nearby Royal Navy destroyer. Before Bond kills him, Safin infects Bond with nanobots that have been programmed to attack Swann and Mathilde. Because of this, Bond decides to sacrifice himself to save them. After a tearful goodbye to Swann, who confirms that Mathilde is in fact his daughter, Bond is killed when the missiles obliterate the factory.[[50]](#cite_note-production_start-52)[[51]](#cite_note-53)

**Uranus** is the seventh [planet](/wiki/Planet "Planet") from the [Sun](/wiki/Sun "Sun"). It is a gaseous [cyan](/wiki/Cyan "Cyan")-coloured [ice giant](/wiki/Ice_giant "Ice giant"). Most of the planet is made of [water](/wiki/Water "Water"), [ammonia](/wiki/Ammonia "Ammonia"), and [methane](/wiki/Methane "Methane") in a [supercritical phase of matter](/wiki/Supercritical_fluid "Supercritical fluid"), which astronomy calls "ice" or [volatiles](/wiki/Volatile_(astrogeology) "Volatile (astrogeology)"). [The planet's atmosphere](/wiki/Atmosphere_of_Uranus "Atmosphere of Uranus") has a complex layered [cloud](/wiki/Cloud "Cloud") structure and has the lowest minimum temperature (49 K (−224 °C; −371 °F)) of all the [Solar System](/wiki/Solar_System "Solar System")'s planets. It has a marked [axial tilt](/wiki/Axial_tilt "Axial tilt") of 82.23° with a [retrograde](/wiki/Retrograde_and_prograde_motion "Retrograde and prograde motion") rotation period of 17 hours and 14 minutes. This means that in an 84-Earth-year [orbital period](/wiki/Orbital_period "Orbital period") around the Sun, its poles get around 42 years of continuous sunlight, followed by 42 years of continuous darkness.

Uranus has the third-largest diameter and fourth-largest mass among the Solar System's planets. Based on current models, inside its volatile [mantle](/wiki/Mantle_(geology) "Mantle (geology)") layer is a rocky core, and a thick [hydrogen](/wiki/Hydrogen "Hydrogen") and [helium](/wiki/Helium "Helium") atmosphere surrounds it. Trace amounts of [hydrocarbons](/wiki/Hydrocarbon "Hydrocarbon") (thought to be produced via [hydrolysis](/wiki/Hydrolysis "Hydrolysis")) and [carbon monoxide](/wiki/Carbon_monoxide "Carbon monoxide") along with [carbon dioxide](/wiki/Carbon_dioxide "Carbon dioxide") (thought to have originated from [comets](/wiki/Comet "Comet")) have been detected in the upper atmosphere. There are many unexplained [climate phenomena in Uranus's atmosphere](/wiki/Climate_of_Uranus "Climate of Uranus"), such as its peak wind speed of 900 km/h (560 mph),[[25]](#cite_note-Sromovsky_&_Fry_2005-31) variations in its polar cap, and its erratic cloud formation.

In the transition to Web 2.0 in the mid-2000s, a number of [research groups](/wiki/Research_group "Research group") emerged aiming to improve the existing infrastructure of the Internet.[[206]](#cite_note-fm-206) These future Internet groups coalesced around the idea that the current Internet and its legacy protocols were inadequate to support the exponential increase in traffic and the integration of mobile technologies.[[207]](#cite_note-survey-207) A number of experimental networking schemes and protocols were developed, seeking to either build upon the existing Internet in an evolutionary approach or to supplant it entirely in a clean-slate approach.[[208]](#cite_note-208) These schemes varied in scope, but usually prioritized enhanced support for mobile networking, [cloud computing](/wiki/Cloud_computing "Cloud computing"), [content delivery](/wiki/Content_delivery "Content delivery"), and [user privacy](/wiki/Internet_privacy "Internet privacy").[[209]](#cite_note-foundation-209)

In 1967, [Alice de Rivera](/wiki/Alice_de_Rivera "Alice de Rivera") sued the Board of Education, alleging that she had been banned from taking Stuyvesant's entrance exam because of her gender.[[23]](#cite_note-24) The lawsuit was decided in her favor, and Stuyvesant was required to accept female students.[[14]](#cite_note-nyclpc-15): 6 The first female students were accepted in September 1969, when Stuyvesant offered admission to 14 girls and enrolled 12 of them.[[17]](#cite_note-nyt199209-18) The next year, Stuyvesant accepted 223 female students.[[14]](#cite_note-nyclpc-15): 6 By 2015, girls were 43% of the student body.[[24]](#cite_note-NYCDOE2016-25)

In 1972, the [New York State Legislature](/wiki/New_York_State_Legislature "New York State Legislature") passed the Hecht–Calandra Act, which designated four citywide selective specialized public high schools in New York City—Stuyvesant, [Brooklyn Technical High School](/wiki/Brooklyn_Technical_High_School "Brooklyn Technical High School"), Bronx Science, and the [High School of Music & Art](/wiki/High_School_of_Music_%26_Art "High School of Music & Art") (now [Fiorello H. LaGuardia High School](/wiki/Fiorello_H._LaGuardia_High_School "Fiorello H. LaGuardia High School"))—as specialized high schools of New York City. The act called for a uniform exam to be administered for admission to Brooklyn Tech, Bronx Science, and Stuyvesant.[[25]](#cite_note-gotham1-26) The exam, named the [Specialized High Schools Admissions Test](/wiki/Specialized_High_Schools_Admissions_Test "Specialized High Schools Admissions Test") (SHSAT), tested the mathematical and verbal abilities of students who were applying to any of the specialized high schools. The only exception was for applicants to the music and arts program at LaGuardia High School, who were accepted by audition rather than examination.[[25]](#cite_note-gotham1-26)

At 1,104,300 square kilometres (426,372.61 sq mi),[[164]](#cite_note-CIA_World_Factbook-167) Ethiopia is the world's 26th-largest country, comparable in size to [Bolivia](/wiki/Bolivia "Bolivia"). The major portion of Ethiopia lies in the [Horn of Africa](/wiki/Horn_of_Africa "Horn of Africa"), which is the easternmost part of the African landmass. The territories that have frontiers with Ethiopia are Eritrea to the north and then, moving in a clockwise direction, Djibouti, Somalia, Kenya, South Sudan and Sudan. Within Ethiopia is a vast highland complex of mountains and dissected plateaus divided by the [Great Rift Valley](/wiki/Great_Rift_Valley,_Ethiopia "Great Rift Valley, Ethiopia"), which runs generally southwest to northeast and is surrounded by lowlands, [steppes](/wiki/Steppe "Steppe"), or semi-desert. There is a great diversity of terrain with wide variations in climate, soils, natural vegetation and settlement patterns.

Ethiopia is an ecologically diverse country, ranging from the deserts along the eastern border to the tropical forests in the south to extensive [Afromontane](/wiki/Afromontane "Afromontane") in the northern and southwestern parts. [Lake Tana](/wiki/Lake_Tana "Lake Tana") in the north is the source of the [Blue Nile](/wiki/Blue_Nile "Blue Nile").
